title: It did not end at 27! Cheers erupted in succession in the fourth round... Sonu, LG, and Samsung made additional selections → KBL draft records most with '30 picks' [Jamsil on-site]

 Players selected at the 2026 KBL Rookie Draft held at Seoul Jamsil Student Gymnasium on the 20th pose for a commemorative photo wearing their respective team uniforms, fists clenched. /Photo=Provided by KBL With only three rounds completed, 27 players were selected, matching the all-time record of most selections set nine years ago. As three more players were called in the fourth round, a record-high 30 players earned professional jerseys at this year's KBL Rookie Draft.
 The KBL held the 2026 KBL Rookie Draft at Seoul Jamsil Student Gymnasium on the 20th. Of the 44th participants, 30 were chosen by professional teams. The selection rate was 68.2%.
 According to the KBL, this is the first time that 30 players have been selected in a single year, excluding the second-division draft. The previous record was set in 2017. That year, exactly like this year, 44 players participated, and 27 of them (61.4%) entered the professional ranks.
 The first player called by name was Lee Dong-geun, a forward from Korea University. Suwon KT, which held the overall first pick, selected Lee Dong-geun. Ulsan Hyundai Mobis picked Kim Seung-woo (Yonsei University) with the second pick, and Seoul SK chose Go Chan-yu (Chung-Ang University) with the third pick. Anyang Jungguanjang selected Gu Min-gyo (Sungkyunkwan University) with the fourth pick, and Daegu Korea Gas Corporation took Lee Ju-young (Yonsei University) with the fifth pick.
 Wonju DB called the name of Lee Chae-hyung (Yonsei University) with the sixth pick, Seoul Samsung picked Sim Ju-eon (Korea University) with the seventh pick, and Changwon LG selected Son Yu-chan (Hanyang University) with the eighth pick. After Goyang Sonu chose Woo Seong-hee (Dongguk University) with the ninth pick, Busan KCC designated Lee Hae-sol (Yonsei University) with the 10th pick, concluding the first round.
 In the second round as well, all 10 teams exercised their draft rights, and 20 players found a team early on. The first team to pass on a selection was DB, holding the sixth pick in the third round. Following this, Samsung selected guard Lee Gun-hee from Korea University, and LG picked center Hong Sang-min from Yonsei University. As Sonu and KCC both passed on their selections, seven players received professional calls in the third round. This brought the total to 27.
 Lee Dong-geun, who wore the Suwon KT jersey as the overall first pick. /Photo=Provided by KBL The team that surpassed the previous record was Sonu, which had passed on selections in the immediately preceding round. When KCC, holding the first pick of the fourth round, passed, Sonu, with the second pick, called the name of guard Yeo Chan-young from Konkuk University. He was the 28th player selected that day. Cheers erupted from the stands, and Yeo Chan-young climbed onto the stage with a relieved smile.
 Immediately following, LG chose guard Baek Seung-hyuk, who played in the second division of college basketball at Dongguk University WISE. This was Baek's second attempt. Having transferred from Dongguk University to Dongguk University WISE last year in search of more playing time, he had been passed over once in that year's draft.
 Nevertheless, he proved his worth by averaging 19.8 points and 12.8 assists per game at this year's MBC Cup National College Basketball Tournament. LG recognized this value and signed Baek Seung-hyuk.
 Lee Kyung-min, who received a selection from Seoul Samsung. /Photo=Provided by KBL The final cheer erupted when it was Samsung's turn. When Samsung selected Lee Kyung-min, the captain of Chung-Ang University, with the fourth pick of the fourth round, this year's total number of selections reached an all-time high of 30. Having previously selected Sim Ju-eon, Kim Seo-won, and Lee Gun-hee, Samsung, along with LG, signed the most rookies among the 10th teams, with four players each.
 The six teams that followed Samsung in turn all passed on their selections. Thus, this year's draft, which began with Lee Dong-geun from Korea University, ended with the name of Lee Kyung-min from Chung-Ang University.
